plain_english: ProPublica is a Pulitzer-winning nonprofit newsroom that spends months on single investigations — opioid money, prisoner treatment, tax-dodging billionaires, and officials whose side deals help companies they once regulated. It endorses no candidate and publishes its evidence as downloadable databases. Its story selection and framing lean left on accountability topics, and its reader community rates it clearly left of center.
voter_impact_translation: This is the outlet that turns public records into tools voters can actually use: searchable detainee case files, follow-the-money charts, and conflict-of-interest papers on both parties' officials — the same evidence-first playbook this site applies to payola.
framing_signature: Long-form document investigations, public-database releases, and accountability stories about money and power that mainstream desks drop after one day.
blindspot_warning: Story selection skews toward harms affecting workers, tenants, and patients; recent politics output concentrates on Republican officeholders, with Democratic officials and legacy media receiving less of the same forensic treatment.
